correctness.rationale: For any finite connected undirected positively weighted Laplacian, a jointly reset subset R with |R|>=2 and nonempty unreset M, kappa>0, lambda>0 and arbitrary fixed real frequency vector, the synchronous-coupling generator has negative definite mean-square drift -2 kappa L-lambda P; thus one invariant law exists and is unique with finite second moments. I reconstructed the Schur-complement mean xbar_R=(lambda I+kappa(H-E^T G^-1 E))^-1 h and centered matrix equation kappa(LC+CL)+lambda(C-JCJ)=lambda(P xbar)(P xbar)^T. If W=C_MM vanishes, zero variance makes X_M pathwise constant; continuity at resets and analyticity of the reset-block ODE force E H^j h=0 for j<r. Conversely Cayley-Hamilton annihilation gives a stationary deterministic unreset block at every rate. Positive definite grounded G and the three covariance block equations give U=lambda^-2 hh^T+O(lambda^-3), V=-kappa lambda^-3 hh^T E^T+O(lambda^-4), and W=lambda^-3 T+O(lambda^-4), GT+TG=2 kappa(Eh)(Eh)^T; the integral Gramian proves rank T=dim span{G^j Eh:0<=j<m}. Explicit reset-star silence, four-vertex cubic-cancellation without silence, and n=4 r=2 full-rank transfer were independently cross-checked numerically at several finite lambda values. Norm bounds are for fixed finite systems only, not graph-uniform or nonlinear sine coupling.
